introduction.definition: A high-pressure reactor carries out reactions such as hydrogenation at high pressure and temperature. Its thick forged body and bolted cover with a metal seal contain the pressure; a magnetic drive stirs without a shaft seal, gas is fed through a sparger, and a coil removes heat. Relief valve and rupture disc protect against over-pressure.

video_tutorials.title: Pressure Reactor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pressure Reactor.
A high-pressure reactor carries out reactions such as hydrogenation at high pressure and temperature.
Its thick forged body and bolted cover with a metal seal contain the pressure; a magnetic drive stirs without a shaft seal, gas is fed through a sparger, and a coil removes heat.
Relief valve and rupture disc protect against over-pressure.
Typical applications include hydrogenation; polymerisation and oxidation under pressure; catalyst testing and R&D; supercritical processes.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Agitator Shaft with Gas-Dispersion (Rushton) Turbines.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Pressure Reactor works.
Liquid is charged and the cover bolted with a metal seal ring.
Gas is fed through the sparger ring at the bottom.
The magnetically driven turbines disperse the gas into the liquid.
The coil removes reaction heat.
Safety valve and rupture disc protect against over-pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Pressure Reactor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pressure Reactor.
Leak test closure before each run.
Replace seal ring; check stud threads.
Re-certify vessel (hydro-test, NDT).
Watch for closure leak: pressure decay. Common cause: damaged seal, uneven bolt torque.
Watch for decoupling of magnetic drive: agitation stops. Common cause: high viscosity, overheating.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
